# Issue 7300 triage

## Assessment

The complete, as-filed repro no longer crashes current `main-debug`. It exits 0
and emits SPIR-V including `NonSemantic.Shader.DebugInfo.100` and ray-query
debug records (`out-main-debug.txt`). The same shader without
`-fspv-debug=vulkan-with-source` also exits 0
(`variant-no-debug-info-main-debug.txt`), providing the requested negative
control.

The measured stable-release fix boundary is **v1.8.2505.1 (crashes) to
v1.9.2602 (succeeds)**. v1.8.2505.1 exits `0xC0000005` and prints the reported
access violation; v1.9.2602 exits 0 and emits SPIR-V. v1.9.2602.24 and
v1.9.2607 also succeed. A linear scan was used because the oldest stable
releases cannot all exercise the option.

The issue is a complete repro and the current status is `does-not-repro`, with
`fixed-in v1.9.2602` as the stable-release history result. Suggested action:
`close-fixed`; the issue is already closed.

## Invalid and excluded probes

- v1.4.1907 is explicitly `invalid-probe`: it reports `SPIR-V CodeGen not
  available`.
- v1.5.2010, v1.6.2104, and v1.6.2106 reject
  `vulkan-with-source` as an unknown debug-info control parameter, so they did
  not run the mode under test. Collation promoted that diagnostic into the
  `invalid-probe` classifier, and these three probes are now stamped
  `invalid-probe` rather than `no-repro`.
- Five probeable prereleases were excluded by stable-release policy:
  v1.5.2003, v1.8.2306-preview, v1.8.2405-mesh-nodes-preview,
  v1.10.2605.2, and v1.10.2605.24.
- The first stable release able to exercise this configuration in the captured
  scan is v1.6.2112; it crashes. Every probeable stable release through
  v1.8.2505.1 crashes.

## Provenance and corroboration

`manual-case-main-debug-version.txt` records the binary's self-reported
fork-local merge `7665270b9`. `manual-case-provenance.txt` records zero changed
paths outside this skill between that source and public commit
`89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df`; the `origin/main^` control detects
`tools/clang/unittests/HLSLExec/LinAlgTests.cpp`.

Compiler Explorer corroborates the history at
https://godbolt.org/z/zbP5qasd3: DXC 1.6.2112 exits 139 (`SIGSEGV`), while
`dxc_trunk` exits 0 and emits SPIR-V. Full panes and the verified link payload
are archived in `manual-case-godbolt-verify.txt`.

The duplicate thread's timeline links commit
`61de7411f952cb0c4b6c73091555dad6419180ee`, whose GET response is archived as
`candidate-commit-61de7411.json`. That commit was then **built and tested
directly**, together with its first parent `b0245e32fdcf412850ed073476669f3a83fa5a76`,
rather than being inferred from ancestry or from the PR text. Both were built as
Release `dxc` from detached worktrees whose submodule pins are identical, so the
only source difference between them is the commit's own 12-line diff
(`case SpirvType::TK_RayQueryKHR:` in `lowerToDebugType`, plus a regression test).
`manual-case-fix-commit.txt`, generated by `measure-fix-commit.py`, records the 2x2:

| build | as-filed repro | same command without `-fspv-debug=vulkan-with-source` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| parent `b0245e32f` (self-reports `1.8.0.5092 (b0245e32f)`) | exit `0xE0000001`, `Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert` | exit 0 |
| commit `61de7411f` (self-reports `1.8.0.5093 (61de7411f)`) | exit 0, emits SPIR-V | exit 0 |

The parent fails only in the mode under test, so the failure is a property of
ray-query debug-type lowering rather than of the build. This identifies
`61de7411f` as the exact fixing commit: its parent still fails and it does not.

The parent's internal failure presents as an assert (`0xE0000001`) in this
locally built binary, where the shipped release binaries present the same defect
as an access violation (`0xC0000005`); both satisfy the `internal_failure`
predicate, which is why the predicate is defined on internal-failure status
rather than on message text.

## Labels

The live labels are `bug`, `spirv`, and `needs-triage`
(`manual-case-live-labels.txt`). The measurements support adding `crash` and
removing `needs-triage`; these are proposals only and were not applied.

There were no attachments on issue 7300. The linked duplicate's proposed patch
was downloaded as `attachment-debug_rayquery.patch`; its complete comments and
timeline were also archived. Issue 7300 has one pre-existing cross-reference,
from the duplicate, and no triage-created event.
